newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle active $64, steady - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle active $64, steady - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle traded actively after midday Wednesday at $64.00 per cwt, unchanged from last week, feedlot sources said.
About 20,000 head sold each in Kansas and the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, with about 40,000 expected by the end of the day, they said.

"I'm a little disappointed we didn't get $65.00, especially after the board (CME live cattle futures) closed higher, but one person jumped at the $64.00 bid and the rest followed," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
August live cattle futures closed up 0.925 cent at 66.700 cents a lb and October was up 0.900 cent at 69.600.
Packer bids through most of the day at $63.00 were rebuffed by owners asking mostly $65.00, with a few at $66.00, they said.
Several feedlot sources said they initally passed on bids at $64.00 after midday, but decided to sell their cattle at that level when momentum started growing.

Fed cattle prices also were underpinned by recent strength in beef prices and smaller numbers of cattle on this week's showlist. Outlooks for gradual declines in cattle supplies through the summer also bolstered prices, they said.
